description: Architectural rules enforcing the Zero-Trust security model, defense-in-depth, least privilege, and strict cryptographic protections.

rules.name: Zero-Trust Perimeter Verification (Explicit Auth Everywhere)
rules.description: Internal microservices and private endpoints must validate authorization tokens (JWT/mTLS) explicitly; assuming internal networks are inherently trusted is prohibited.
rules.rationale: Compromised internal lateral movement is the primary threat in modern distributed attacks. Every service must verify caller identity and permissions.
rules.remediation: Apply authentication & RBAC authorization interceptors/guards to all private endpoints.

rules.name: Mandatory Input Sanitization & Content-Type Enforcement
rules.description: All request payloads must be strictly validated against strong schemas before reaching domain logic, and Content-Type headers must be strictly enforced.
rules.rationale: Prevents injection vulnerabilities (XSS, Command Injection, Prototype Pollution) at the earliest ingestion stage.
rules.remediation: Use validation DTOs/Zod schemas with unknown field stripping and explicit Content-Type verification.

rules.name: Audit Logging for All Mutation Operations
rules.description: Any state-modifying action (create, update, delete, permission escalation) must generate structured, immutable audit log events containing caller ID, action, timestamp, and target resource ID.
rules.rationale: Mandatory for regulatory compliance (SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA) and forensic security auditing.
rules.remediation: Emit structured audit events from domain handlers to secure audit logs.

rules.name: No Insecure Cryptographic Primitives
rules.description: Prohibits using deprecated cryptographic algorithms (e.g. MD5, SHA1 for signatures/passwords, DES, RC4) or weak random number generators for security tokens.
rules.rationale: Vulnerable algorithms can be cracked or collided with minimal computational effort.
rules.remediation: Use modern cryptographic standards: Argon2id / bcrypt for passwords, AES-256-GCM for encryption, SHA-256/SHA-512 for hashing, and cryptographically secure PRNGs.
